title: Ooze
summary: OOZE, verb intransitive ooz. [The origin of this word is not easily ascertained. Heb. See Issue.] To flow gently; to percolate, as a liquid through the pores of a substance, or through small openings.

inlines.v: OOZE, verb intransitive ooz. [The origin of this word is not easily ascertained. Heb. See Issue.] To flow gently; to percolate, as a liquid through the pores of a substance, or through small openings. Water oozes from the earth and through a filter. The latent rill, scaree oozing through the grass. OOZE, noun 1. Soft mud or slime; earth so wet as to flow gently or easily yield to pressure. 2. Soft flow; spring. 3. The liquor of a tan-vat.
